description: A composite figure group for LDSs in 3.5 wt% NaCl, combining one data table with two panels. The table lists EIS fitting parameters after potentiostatic polarization — R_s (Ω·cm²), Q_1 (Ω⁻¹·cm⁻²·sⁿ), n_1, R_1 (Ω·cm²), Q_2 (Ω⁻¹·cm⁻²·sⁿ), n_2, R_2 (Ω·cm²) and R_p (Ω·cm²) — for S0, S950, S1050 and S1150; R_s is nearly constant (6.34–6.52) while R_p peaks for S950 (21355) versus S0 (6143). Panel (a) is a Mott–Schottky plot of C⁻² (×10⁹ F⁻²·cm⁴, ordinate 0–8) against E (V vs. SCE, −1.2 to −0.4) with four curves (S0 red stars, S950 green circles, S1050 blue triangles, S1150 magenta squares); a dashed vertical line near −0.96 V separates Region 1 (positive slope, n-type) from Region 2 (negative slope, p-type). S950 reaches the highest C⁻² maximum (near 6 on the ordinate) and S0 the lowest (near 3.8). Panel (b) is a bar chart of N_D and N_A (×10²¹/cm³) with printed values: S0 0.70/2.25, S950 0.26/0.68, S1050 0.38/1.03, S1150 0.49/1.25. Together the panels argue that S950 forms the least defective, most protective oxide film.

subfigures.description: EIS fitting-parameter table with columns R_s (Ω·cm²), Q_1 (Ω⁻¹·cm⁻²·sⁿ), n_1, R_1 (Ω·cm²), Q_2 (Ω⁻¹·cm⁻²·sⁿ), n_2, R_2 (Ω·cm²) and R_p (Ω·cm²) for samples S0, S950, S1050 and S1150. R_p values are 6143, 21355, 14144 and 10756 Ω·cm² respectively.

Mott–Schottky plot of C⁻² (×10⁹ F⁻²·cm⁴, 0–8) versus E (V vs. SCE, −1.2 to −0.4) for S0 (red stars), S950 (green circles), S1050 (blue triangles), S1150 (magenta squares). A pink dashed line near −0.96 V separates Region 1 (n-type, positive slope, peaked curve) from Region 2 (p-type, near-flat slightly negative slope).
Bar chart of carrier densities N_D (purple) and N_A (teal) in ×10²¹/cm³ for S0, S950, S1050 and S1150 with the numeric value printed above each bar: 0.70/2.25, 0.26/0.68, 0.38/1.03, 0.49/1.25.

observations.observation: The table lists EIS fitting parameters R_s, Q_1, n_1, R_1, Q_2, n_2, R_2 and R_p for the samples S0, S950, S1050 and S1150.

R_s is essentially constant across samples (6.50, 6.34, 6.45 and 6.52 Ω·cm² for S0, S950, S1050 and S1150), while R_p differs strongly: 6143, 21355, 14144 and 10756 Ω·cm² respectively, S950 being the highest.
Panel (a) plots C⁻² (×10⁹ F⁻²·cm⁴) against potential E (V vs. SCE) from −1.2 to −0.4, with four curves labelled S0, S950, S1050 and S1150.

In panel (a) a pink dashed vertical line near −0.96 V divides the plot into 'Region 1' (left, rising positive-slope branch) and 'Region 2' (right, descending to a flat, slightly negative-slope branch).
In panel (a) the S950 curve attains the highest C⁻² maximum of the four curves (touching the 6 gridline of the ordinate), while S0 attains the lowest maximum (just below 4).
Panel (b) is a bar chart of N_D and N_A (×10²¹/cm³) with each bar value printed: S0 = 0.70 (N_D) and 2.25 (N_A); S950 = 0.26 and 0.68; S1050 = 0.38 and 1.03; S1150 = 0.49 and 1.25.
The S0 sample shows the highest N_D (0.70 ×10²¹/cm³) and the highest N_A (2.25 ×10²¹/cm³) of all four samples.
The S950 sample shows the lowest N_D (0.26 ×10²¹/cm³) and the lowest N_A (0.68 ×10²¹/cm³) of all four samples.

The caption states the table gives fitting parameters of the EIS of the LDSs after potentiostatic polarization, and that Fig. 12 contains (a) Mott–Schottky curves and (b) the N_D and N_A curves of LDSs in 3.5 wt% NaCl solution.

The citing text states Region 1 spans −1.13 V to −0.93 V_SCE with a positive slope (n-type, dominated by cation interstitials and oxygen vacancies) and Region 2 spans −0.93 V_SCE to −0.67 V_SCE with a negative slope (p-type, cation vacancies).
The citing text states the n-type behaviour of the LDS oxide film is mainly controlled by Al2O3 and Fe2O3, and the p-type behaviour mainly by FeO.
The citing text states that lower N_D and N_A correspond to fewer structural defects and reduced chloride-ion penetration pathways, so the S950 oxide film is the most protective.
The citing text states that although solution treatment generally increases N_D and N_A with increasing grain size, all treated samples maintain lower values than S0.
